facts.detail: Voucher management information is combined with supplier Ready For Service data.
Only voucher submissions meeting quality checks are used.
Superfast suppliers provide cumulative quarterly delivery reports.
Final Superfast data is expected 40 working days after quarter end.
Rounded or invalid UPRNs and future dates can require manual cleansing.
BDUK aims to reduce the overall publication lag to six weeks.
BDUK and Ofcom premises bases differ.
BDUK’s base includes child premises such as flats in houses of multiple occupation.
Voucher data relating to individuals is subject to confidentiality controls.
Historical values can be revised when supplier data quality improves.

facts.detail: BDUK published the quarterly QMI on 24 July 2025.
The reference area is the United Kingdom.
The data covers April 2012 through December 2024.
Quarterly data is presented from April to December 2024.
BDUK validates supplier-returned UPRNs.
A 5% attrition rate is applied to expected-premises data.
At the release date, 66% of voucher premises used the direct methodology.
The remaining 34% were estimated using multipliers.
The multiplier method uses an 18% attrition adjustment.
GIS reporting excludes premises already built by another supplier.

facts.detail: BDUK published the Shared Rural Network evaluation plan on 15 August 2025.
Ipsos UK and partners were commissioned to undertake the evaluation.
The programme involves EE, Three, Virgin Media O2 and Vodafone.
The programme aims for 4G coverage from at least one operator across 95% of UK landmass.
The programme aims to extend coverage to at least 280,000 additional premises.
The programme aims to extend coverage across 16,000 km of roads.
The evaluation distinguishes Partial Not Spots, Extended Area Service and Total Not Spots components.
The plan describes 292 Emergency Services Network masts for possible commercial use.
The recommended approach includes process, impact and economic evaluation.
The plan proposes matching and difference-in-differences methods for counterfactual analysis.

facts.detail: BDUK published the GigaHubs Process Review Summary on 26 June 2026.
Belmana and GC Insight conducted the review.
The intervention connects remote public buildings such as schools, GP surgeries and libraries.
GigaHubs delivered approximately 1,200 Hub connections during 2021–26.
Delivery occurred through six projects.
BDUK had delivered 5,670 Hubs by September 2025.
Evidence included BDUK management data and stakeholder interviews.
The review examined initiation, scoping, procurement and delivery stages.
Local delivery capability was identified as a critical determinant of progress.
Modelling indicated around 30–60 local authorities could have enough sites to lead projects.

facts.detail: BDUK published the annual report and accounts on 21 November 2023.
The report covers 1 April 2022 to 31 March 2023.
BDUK became an executive agency on 1 April 2022.
The report identifies Project Gigabit and the Shared Rural Network as the two major programmes.
BDUK reported exceeding its Project Gigabit delivery target.
BDUK reported passing 162,600 premises with gigabit-capable broadband during the year.
Cumulative gigabit delivery reached 929,700 premises.
Project Gigabit is described as a £5 billion programme.
The sponsor department moved from DCMS to DSIT at the end of the year.
The Comptroller and Auditor General audited the financial statements.
